newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-GOALKEEPERS STAR IN MEDAL ROUND GAMES.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-GOALKEEPERS STAR IN MEDAL ROUND GAMES.

text.p: Goalkeepers stole the show as Canada beat Finland 1-0 and Russia drew 1-1 with the United States in the ice hockey world championship medal round on Tuesday.

The results left Russia alone at the top of the standings on five points ahead of Sweden and Canada, both on four. For the United States, winners of the inaugural Word Cup last autumn, the draw meant they can no longer reach this year's world championship final.
The United States have only one game left, against Finland on Friday, and cannot reach the final even if they win and advance to five points.
Russia, too, have only one game left in the medal round. They play Canada on Friday.
Russian netminder Maxim Mikhailovsky made 24 saves and U.S. goaltender Chris Terreri parried 38 shots in a closely fought game.

The U.S. took the lead late in the second period, Calgary Flames forward Marty McInnis opening the scoring assisted by Boston Bruins centre Ted Donato, whose pass found its way past Mikhailovsky to let McInnis hit an empty net.
Terreri withstood a barrage of shots, 16 in the third period, while Russia attacked incessantly.

The one puck he failed to save came from a lose shot by 20-year old Russian Alexei Morozov, who broke through in the middle after Alexander Prokopyev had capitalised on a defensive blunder by the U.S. just six minutes before the end of the game.
"We won one point today," relieved Russian coach Igor Dimitryev said.
Jeff Friesen of the San Jose Sharks scored with just over three minutes remaining to lift Canada to a key 1-0 win over Finland earlier on Tuesday.
Friesen, taking a perfect feed from Chris Gratton at the blueline, charged down the slot and held on to the puck until he was on top of Jarmo Myllys then muscled it past the Finnish netminder.
"Our goal was to have 13,250 Finnish fans standing quiet listening to 47 Canadians sing the national anthem at the end of the game," said Canadian coach Andy Murray.
"Unfortunately only two will play for the gold medal so tomorrow we'll have to win a very tough game against the Czech Republic," he said.
The game was a goaltenders' duel between Myllys and Hartford Whalers's Sean Burke, who made two dazzling saves in the dying seconds to preserve the win.
It was the third shutout of the tournament for Burke, who turned aside all 23 shots directed at him by the Finns.
"The score is an indication of the quality of the goaltending we saw today," said Murray. "Both Myllys and Burke were outstanding."
